risks: no ground-truth column appears in the feature list
splits are chronological with a purge gap; the test period is 2025-03-23 12:00:00 onwards
sensor dropouts blank all channels together on 1.99% of rows; imputation is forward-fill with a train-median fallback
0.95% of rows are downtime and must be excluded from both training and scoring
recommendations: use PR-AUC (not accuracy or ROC-AUC) to select models: at 1.13% positives, accuracy is uninformative
subsample negatives for training only; score on the untouched distribution

ablate raw against engineered features rather than trusting these correlations: the best engineered feature gains only +0.000 marginally, but marginal correlation cannot see the interaction that matters here (vibration rising *while load stays flat*)
channels are strongly autocorrelated at 1 h lag -- sequence models are worth testing against a tabular baseline
lookback of 36 samples (6 h) covers the 6 h horizon without spanning typical downtime blocks
13 features carry almost no marginal signal (|corr| < 0.005), e.g. ['pressure_std_1h', 'pressure_std_6h', 'ambient_temp']
data_scientist.headline: 345,600 rows across 80 machines at 10 min resolution; 1.13% positive.

experiments.name: threshold rule on vibration / temperature / current
experiments.learning: Establishes the operating point the plant already has.

experiments.name: xgboost on raw features
experiments.learning: PR-AUC 0.3099 vs baseline 0.1446 (+0.1653). Trees on raw channels already beat the alarm rule, so most of the baseline's weakness was the fixed threshold, not the sensors.

experiments.name: xgboost on engineered features
experiments.learning: PR-AUC 0.5072 vs raw features 0.3099 (+0.1973). Causal rolling statistics and load/ambient normalisation are worth more than any change of architecture tried below.

experiments.name: LSTM on raw channels
experiments.learning: PR-AUC 0.3640 vs best tabular 0.5072 (-0.1432). Learning the temporal structure from raw sequence does not beat handing a tree the same structure explicitly.

experiments.name: LSTM on engineered channels
experiments.learning: PR-AUC 0.5542 vs best tabular 0.5072 (+0.0470). The sequence view finds structure the tabular one misses.

experiments.name: TFT on engineered channels
experiments.learning: PR-AUC 0.5583 vs LSTM 0.5542. No material gain over the LSTM at this data scale -- the extra capacity is not paying for itself.

experiments.name: ensemble lstm_engineered + tft_engineered
experiments.learning: PR-AUC 0.5855 vs best member 0.5583. The blend adds real signal.

selection.name: ensemble lstm_engineered + tft_engineered
selection.rationale: ensemble lstm_engineered + tft_engineered selected on validation PR-AUC 0.5855 (+0.0272 over TFT on engineered channels)
